questions.q: Why isn't KILLing the blocking session a real fix?
options: It would recur every morning and could leave appointment data in an inconsistent, partially-applied state
KILL is not a valid T-SQL command in Azure SQL Database
It fixes the problem permanently with no downsides
It only works on dbo.Invoices, not dbo.Appointments
questions.explain: Killing the session is a workaround for the symptom, not the cause, and risks leaving data in a bad state mid-transaction.

questions.q: What is the actual root cause Lesson 8 found?
options: The transaction stays open across a slow, unrelated step (sending confirmation messages) that doesn't need database locks
The UPDATE statement itself is missing an index
dbo.Appointments has no primary key
The scheduling application never opens a transaction at all
questions.explain: The transaction remains open while an external, slow messaging step runs, holding locks far longer than the actual data change needs.

options: Commit the UPDATE immediately, then send messages after the commit, outside any open transaction
Add more CPU cores to the Azure SQL Database
Change the UPDATE to a DELETE followed by an INSERT
Increase the transaction isolation level to SERIALIZABLE
questions.explain: Committing right after the data change releases locks immediately; sending messages afterward never holds a database transaction open.

questions.q: How do you confirm the fix actually worked?
options: Re-run the blocking-chain query from Lesson 8 and confirm no sustained blocking remains
Ask the scheduling staff if they feel like it's faster
Check that the CREATE INDEX statement from Lesson 7 succeeded
Confirm the batch job's execution plan shows an Index Seek
questions.explain: Re-testing with the same sys.dm_exec_requests query shows blocking is gone or reduced to brief, self-resolving waits.

questions.q: Why does this specific fix generalize beyond this one scenario?
options: A slow, non-database step ending up inside a transaction boundary out of convenience is one of the most common real causes of blocking
It only applies to healthcare scheduling systems specifically
It requires Azure SQL Database's Elastic Jobs feature to work
It is unique to this one stored procedure and doesn't apply elsewhere
questions.explain: Moving slow, unrelated operations (file I/O, API calls, messaging) outside the transaction boundary is a widely applicable fix for blocking.
